title: Refurbishment and Rotation Pipeline for Aging GPU Repopulation
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a proposed pipeline to refurbish and rotate aging GPUs back into regional pools or into lower-tier burst lanes to extend usable capacity, reduce new-order pressure, and smooth lead-time cliffs. Not a final procurement plan — draft for feedback from procurement, SRE, and site reliability teams.

Context / why this matters: 
- Lead times for new H100/A100 orders remain volatile (6-20+ weeks depending on vendor and region).
- We have a trailing cohort of ~1.8k GPUs approaching 36+ months that still test within spec but have lower warranty and higher failure incidence in production.
- Refurbish + redeploy can: 1) reduce net new orders by offsetting 10-25% of near-term demand, 2) provide short-term regional coverage for burst lanes, 3) lower depreciation curve impact if we salvage usable dies.

Scope:
- Focus on EMEA and US-West regional pools where lead-time risk and utilization spikes are highest.
- Run a 12-week pilot processing up to 150 units/week. Mix: older A100-40GB, A10, L4. Avoid H100s in pilot unless vendor-certified refurb flow exists.

High-level pipeline (process flow):
1) Triage -> Inventory pull (data team flags eligible GPUs based on: age, error logs, PUE incidents)
2) Burn-in + diagnostics (48h stress + SMART logs + thermal profiling)
3) Repair & Replace (fans, TIM, thermal pads, reballing outsourced as needed)
4) Binning & labeling (Tier A: full warranty-equivalent; Tier B: limited-burst; Tier C: recycle/parts)
5) Regional redeploy routing (Tier A -> Dedicated pool refill; Tier B -> Burst lanes; Tier C -> sell / recycle)
6) Post-deploy monitoring + 30d regression checks

Throughput & capacity assumptions (pilot):
- Arrival processing capacity: up to 150 units/week at central refurb bench (2 techs + 1 temp contractor)
- Burn-in time: 48 hours typical (pipeline must have 72h buffer for rework)
- Expected Tier A yield: 45% (conservative), Tier B yield: 30%, scrap: 25%
- Cost per unit refurb (parts + labor + test time): $420 (target) vs. new unit delta (A100-40GB) ~ $12k — significant CAPEX avoidance if yield holds

Example calculation (12-week pilot):
- Units processed: 150 * 12 = 1800 units
- Tier A ~ 810 units (45%) -> can offset near-term new orders for Dedicated
- Tier B ~ 540 units -> burst/regional lanes (lower SLA, cheaper run-hours)
- Scrap ~ 450 units -> part harvesting/resale/recycle
- Net effective offset: 810 units new-order avoidance (~6.75% of annual expected new orders of 12k, illustrative)

Operational considerations / SRE constraints:
- Warranty and SLA: Tier A refurbished units will run in non-customer-isolated Dedicated pools only after acceptance tests. For privacy-regulated customers we maintain new-only policy.
- Telemetry: Must tag refurbished units in fleet DB (tags: refurb-date, bin-tier, refurb-batch-id, origin-rack).
- Rollback: Maintain hot-swap lanes and automatic fallback to cloud burst if refurbished instance fails initial 30d health checks.
- Monitoring thresholds: 3x baseline PDUs for GPU temp variance => immediate retire.

Logistics & vendor interactions: 
- Certification partners: Evaluate 1-2 third-party refurbishment labs near EU/US-West to offload heavy reballing. RFP in week 1 of pilot.
- Spare parts procurement: Fans, heatsink pads, power connectors stock target: 1.2x weekly throughput (i.e., parts for ~180 units/week to avoid blocking).
- Shipping windows: 5 business days inbound/outbound for EU labs; for US-West vendor preferred next-day courier (higher cost but reduces pipeline hang).

Risk matrix (top items):
- Unexpected failure rate post-deploy (mitigation: extended burn-in + A/B deploy with canary fraction 5%)
- Regulatory/customer pushback (mitigation: explicit tagging + never place refurbished in regulated VPCs)
- Cost of refurb > benefit (mitigation: weekly cost review vs spot new-order pricing, stop if >60% of new cost)
- Spare parts shortage (mitigation: prioritize parts PO + small buffer on fast ship)

Open questions / decisions needed: 
- Target refurbished warranty offering? (option A: 90-day internal warranty; option B: 180-day extended testing to provide quasi-warranty)
- Where do refurbished Tier A units live in rollouts? (dedicated-only vs mixed pools)
- Escrow / accounting: how to amortize salvage value and OPEX of refurb into forecasting models? finance + accounting input needed.

Pilot timeline (12 weeks):
- Week 0: kickoff, finalize SOP, sign NDA with third-party lab, parts PO
- Week 1-2: dry-run with 100 units, iterate test steps, validate tags and DB flows
- Week 3-10: steady-state processing, weekly yield review, adjust parts and shipping lanes
- Week 11-12: final batch + write pilot report, decision meeting (scale / stop)

Success metrics (for pilot go/no-go):
- Tier A yield >= 40% AND cost per refurbished unit <= $650 -> consider scale
- Post-deploy 30d failure rate for Tier A <= 2x baseline failure rate for new units
- Net new-order avoidance >= 10% of planned Q1-Q2 orders (measured in usable-capacity-equivalent)

Action items (owners):
- Procurement: prepare rapid PO template for parts and two lab RFPs (Owner: Ravi Kumar)
- SRE/Telemetry: add refurb tag schema + alert playbook (Owner: Samir Patel)
- Legal: draft refurbished-lab NDA + SLA checklist for third-party labs (Owner: Jia Li)
- Ops: confirm crate flow and staging bench capacity for 150 units/week (Owner: Elena Martinez)

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This doc intentionally keeps numbers conservative. If vendor quotes for refurb fall lower, this becomes much more attractive.
- We should evaluate a parallel experiment for on-prem light reballing vs full lab send-out — mix might reduce cost and lead time for certain failure classes.
- Slack thread that started this: #gpu-life-cycle -> pinned messages on tests and failure classes (see linked_artifacts)

Appendix: quick diagnostic checklist (burn-in):
- 48h synthetic load (mix of infer + mem-bound kernels)
- SMART + ECC error scan (zero tolerance for persistent ECC)
- Thermal ramp test (idle -> 95% load ramp, check throttling)
- Power draw profile vs baseline (>=10% variance => flag)

End.
